summary.short: Amends Minnesota criminal law (Minn. Stat. 609.771) on deep fakes used to influence elections. It sets the elements of the dissemination offence and its penalties, adds candidate forfeiture and disqualification, and takes effect July 1, 2024.
summary.long: Sections 76 and 77 of this act amend Minnesota Statutes 609.771 on the use of deep fakes to influence an election. Under amended subdivision 2, a person who disseminates a deep fake, or agrees to disseminate one, commits a crime if the person knows or reasonably should know, with reckless disregard as to whether the item is a deep fake, that the dissemination is made without the depicted individual's consent and with intent to injure a candidate or influence an election. The dissemination must also fall within stated periods: within 90 days before an election, within 90 days before a political party nominating convention, or after the start of the absentee voting period before a presidential nomination primary or a regular or special state or local primary or general election. Subdivision 2(b) exempts a broadcaster or cable system that disseminates a candidate's deep fake where federal law requires the dissemination. Subdivision 3 sets penalties: for a violation within five years of a prior conviction, up to five years' imprisonment or a fine of up to $10,000; for a violation with intent to cause violence or bodily harm, up to 364 days or a fine of up to $3,000; otherwise up to 90 days or a fine of up to $1,000. A candidate convicted of a violation must receive a supplemental judgment declaring forfeiture of the nomination or office under section 211B.17, and a convicted candidate or individual is disqualified from appointment to office under section 211B.18. The section is effective July 1, 2024 and applies to crimes committed on or after that date. obligations.summary: Any person may not disseminate a deep fake, or enter into a contract or agreement to disseminate one, where the person knows or reasonably should know, with reckless disregard, that it is a deep fake, it is made without the depicted individual's consent, it is made with intent to injure a candidate or influence an election, and it takes place within the amended time windows (within 90 days before an election, or after the start of the absentee voting period before specified primaries or elections, or within 90 days before a nominating convention). Subd. 2(b) exempts a broadcaster or cable system disseminating a candidate's deep fake where federal law requires it. Amends Minn. Stat. 609.771, subd. 2.
